title: pyflam: open, multiplatform wildfire-behavior modelling (weather-driven and fire-atmosphere coupled)
description: pyflam is an open-source, cross-platform Python toolkit for wildfire-behavior modelling for management, planning and suppression. It implements the Rothermel (1972) surface fire-spread model and the standard fuel models, minimum-travel-time fire growth with a selectable anisotropic-Eikonal (Finsler) alternative, random-ignition burn probability, a literature-current crown-fire model, physics-based ember spotting, weather-driven per-cell fuel-moisture conditioning (GFS/ERA5), native terrain-wind solvers and a buoyant-CFD plume for coupled fire-atmosphere pyroconvection, and FlamMap/FARSITE .lcp I/O. pyflam is an independent implementation built from published, peer-reviewed fire science and contains no FlamMap code.
